Alternative 2 Comparison to Proposed Project Summary
The Shortened Breakwater Alternative would generally result in overall similar environmental
impacts compared to the proposed project (see Table 5-2). By shortening the breakwater,
construction-related impacts would be reduced slightly, including construction-related impacts
related to air quality, biological resources, hydrology and water quality, and noise. Nonetheless,
under this Alternative, the same mitigation identified for the proposed project would be required.
Overall, operation-related impacts would remain the same. Overall, this alternative would advance
the basic project objectives of enhancing public access and recreational opportunities at the
Berkeley Waterfront and providing efficient and environmentally friendly zero emission public ferry
service between Berkeley and San Francisco. However, this alternative would meet the project
objective (related to enhancing public access and recreational opportunities at the Berkeley
Waterfront) to a slightly lesser extent than the proposed project due to the reduced length of the
breakwater. It should be noted that the primary purpose of the breakwater is to provide a safe
harbor for ferry vessels, and the public access that it provides is a secondary purpose.

Alternative 3 Comparison to Proposed Project Summary
The Shortened Pier Alternative would generally result in overall similar environmental impacts
compared to the proposed project (see Table 5-2). By shortening the pier, construction-related
impacts would be reduced slightly, including construction-related impacts related to air quality,
biological resources, hydrology and water quality, and noise. Nonetheless, under this Alternative,
the same mitigation identified for the proposed project would be required. Overall, operation-
related impacts would remain the same. Overall, this alternative would advance the basic project
objectives of enhancing public access and recreational opportunities at the Berkeley Waterfront and
providing efficient and environmentally friendly zero emission public ferry service between Berkeley
and San Francisco. However, this alternative would meet the project objective (related to enhancing
public access and recreational opportunities at the Berkeley Waterfront) to a slightly lesser extent
than the proposed project due to the reduced length of the pier. It should be noted that the primary
purpose of the pier beyond the breakwater is to provide enhanced public access and recreational
opportunities. Unlike the breakwater that has a dual purpose of providing a safe harbor for ferry
vessels and providing public access/recreational opportunities; or the portion of the pier from the
public plaza to the breakwater, which has the dual purpose of providing access to ferry vessels and
public access/recreational opportunities; the portion of the pier beyond the breakwater’s sole
purpose is provide public access/recreational opportunities.

Alternative 4 Comparison to Proposed Project Summary
The Reduced Landside Facilities Alternative would generally result in overall similar environmental
impacts compared to the proposed project (see Table 5-2). By reducing the number of facilities to
be installed, construction-related and excavation-related impacts would be reduced slightly,
including construction-related and excavation-related impacts related to aesthetics, biological
resources, cultural resources, geology and soils, hazards and hazardous materials, hydrology and
water quality, noise, recreation, tribal cultural resources, and utilities and service systems. Overall,
operation-related impacts would remain the same; however, this Alternative 4 could result in
slightly greater operational impacts related to air quality, GHG emissions, land use and planning,
and transportation, due to the potential for the project site to be used by less visitors compared to
the proposed project because of its reduced attractiveness with less amenities. Overall, this
alternative would advance the basic project objectives of enhancing public access and recreational



5-30
                                                                                            Alternatives



opportunities at the Berkeley Waterfront and providing efficient and environmentally friendly zero
emission public ferry service between Berkeley and San Francisco. However, this alternative would
meet the project objective (related to enhancing public access and recreational opportunities at the
Berkeley Waterfront) to a slightly lesser extent than the proposed project due to the reduction in
facilities. Under Alternative 4, people using the Berkeley Waterfront would not be able to use a
cycle track to access the project site; would not be able to congregate in a public plaza; would not
be able to use the Bay Trail Extension off Seawall Drive; and overall, would not be able to enjoy the
Bay as much as under the proposed project.

5.10.2 Identification of Environmentally Superior Alternative
The proposed project as well as any of the alternatives considered would provide environmental
benefits, such as reductions in VMT that would not be realized under the No Project Alternative
(Alternative 1). While Alternative 1 would avoid certain construction-related impacts of the
proposed project, it would not meet basic project objectives and is not considered the
environmentally superior alternative, because it would not provide the long-term environmental
benefits of new ferry service (i.e., reduced VMT, reduced air quality emissions, reduced GHG
emissions).
The proposed project and Alternatives 2 through 4 would all provide the long-term environmental
benefits of new ferry service. Overall, the proposed project and Alternatives 2 and 3 would result in
the same long-term environmental benefits of new ferry service, because operation would be
similar. The long-term environmental benefits of new ferry service under Alternative 4 are expected
to be slightly reduced compared to the proposed project, since patrons may opt to use ferry service
less if there are fewer landside amenities. Nonetheless, Alternative 4 is still expected to provide
long-term environmental benefits of new ferry service.
In comparing Alternatives 2 through 4, the main difference relates to the extent in which these
alternatives would reduce construction-related impacts. Table 5-2 identifies that Alternatives 2 and
3 would reduce five construction-related environmental impacts (related to air quality, biological
resources, GHG emissions, hydrology and water quality, and noise) and that Alternative 4 would
reduce ten environmental impacts (related to aesthetics, biological resources, cultural resources,
geology and soils, hazards and hazardous materials, hydrology and water quality, noise, recreation,
tribal cultural resources, and utilities and service systems) while increasing 4 environmental impacts
(related to air quality, GHG emissions, land use and planning, and transportation).
Overall, Alternative 4 would have a greater reduction in construction-related impacts compared to
the proposed project and other alternatives, still meet the basic project objectives, and still provide
long-term environmental benefits of new ferry service (albeit potentially to a slightly lesser extent
than Alternatives 2 and 3). Therefore, of the alternatives evaluated in this EIR chapter, Alternative 4
(Reduced Landside Facilities Alternative) would be the environmentally superior alternative.
